L3Harris Technologies Inc. is the only vendor with unique capabilities, experience, expertise, 
and relationships to satisfy the Government's requirements of the test program sets (TPS) for 
these highly specialized items.  
  
L3Harris Technologies Inc. is the original designer and developer of the AN/ALQ-172 
Countermeasures System. They are currently on contract for the AN/ALQ-172 redesigns of 
LRUs -1, 2, 4, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12, 21 and Radio Frequency Interface Unit (RFIU). The Government 
Furnished Equipment (GFE) accountable under contract FA8522-18-C-0001 required for the 
redesign effort and development of the TPS is located at L3Harris Technologies Inc.  
 
The Government does not possess a full technical data package for the AN/ALQ-172(V) System. 
A contractor must have access to the technical data and have extensive knowledge and expertise 
of the AN/ALQ-172 system in order to complete this effort.  Due to the lack of completed 
functional/interface specifications between the LRUs, system knowledge and experience will be 
required in order to properly stimulate Radio Frequency (RF) and digital and analog signals 
between the UUTs. A vendor must have expertise on the ALQ-172 theory of operation, greatly 
above the knowledge of a generic radar or Circuit Card Assembly level expertise. L3Harris 
Technologies Inc. is the only vendor that possesses the knowledge and expertise of the 
redesigned AN/ALQ-172 Countermeasures System.  
  
Harris Corporation is currently developing a Form Fit Function and Interface (FFFI) replacement 
for the LRU hardware. The development contract(s) will result in qualified prototypes and 
delivery of full Level-3 technical data package for each redesigned LRU. The Government will 
have full data rights to compete future acquisition of LRU production units. 
 
The LRUs (LRU-1, 2, 4, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12, 21 and RFIU) are highly specialized to the AN/ALQ-172 
system because the AN/ALQ-172 system provides Situational Awareness (SA) and Self-
Protection (SP) capabilities to large aircraft such as B-52. This is a unique capability for the B-52 
and C-130 aircraft defense against threats. The AN/ALQ-172 Electronic Countermeasures 
(ECM) System has been upgraded over the last 40+ years since its inception in the early 1970s. 
The system architecture is comprised of three (3) subsystems, pulse (LRU-1 and 2), PD/CW 
(LRU-4 and 10) and antenna (LRU-7, 8, and 9), in order to meet its requirements with a 
significantly reduced number of LRUs. The small footprint of the system requirement resulted in 
a distributed processing architecture between the subsystems, each performing specialized 
functions while collaborating with other subsystems. Therefore, internal system interfaces, and 
other timing requirements between subsystems, LRUs and SRUs are critical factors for the 
proper integration and full operations of the system. Harris Corporation is the only vendor who 
has knowledge of the critical factors required to make the system fully operational.  
 
Accordingly, L3Harris Technologies Inc. is the only firm capable of providing the production 
units described in Section III above without the U.S. Air Force experiencing substantial 
duplication in cost and unacceptable delays that is not expected to be recovered through reverse 
engineering the legacy unit.
